claims.text: Instrumented nanoindentation can measure localized hardness and elastic modulus in FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The FeNiCrMn alloy is homogenized into a single-phase high-entropy solid solution after synthesis by methods such as arc melting.
Using polished surfaces and controlled loading rates improves reproducibility and minimizes surface artifacts in nanoindentation.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the single-phase solid solution in FeNiCrMn.
The stabilized solid solution promotes a uniform distribution of the constituent elements.
The entropy-stabilized microstructure resists dislocation motion.
The entropy-stabilized microstructure resists local deformation.
Resistance to dislocation motion and local deformation enhances the intrinsic mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn at the microscale.
FeNiCrMn will have higher nanoindentation hardness than conventional reference alloys with similar processing or microstructures.
FeNiCrMn will have a higher elastic modulus than conventional reference alloys with similar processing or microstructures.
Localized nanoindentation properties will show relatively little spatial variation because the microstructure is stable and uniform.
Nanoindentation responses may not fully represent the alloy's bulk tensile behavior.
Testing temperature may affect the measured mechanical properties.
Scale effects and sample-preparation variability may affect the measured magnitude of mechanical-property enhancement.
